analysis.title: USD Rates Chart Pack: Futures Positions & Curve Analysis
key_insights: Chart pack from CACIB US Rates Strategy (Alex Li) dated 23/11/2026 covering CFTC Commitment of Traders positioning in Treasury, SOFR, Fed funds and equity index futures, plus swap and Treasury curve and butterfly levels.
Non-commercial net positions in Treasury futures are net short across all contracts: TU -983.6K, FV -1,289.1K, TY -1,048.9K, UXY -159.0K, US -3.3K, WN -369.6K.
Non-commercial 3M SOFR net position is -2,606.0K, while 1M SOFR is +58.4K and 30-day Fed funds +5.8K.
Non-commercial equity index futures positions: E-Mini S&P 500 -94.0K and Nasdaq 100 +4.3K.

By trader type as of 17/11/2026, asset managers are net long and leveraged funds net short in Treasury futures. Example: 5Y AM 3,270.8K vs leveraged -2,482.4K (column order inferred from the 5Y/10Y panels), consistent with a basis-trade style pattern.
Swap curve levels on 20/11/2026: 2s10s 3.7bp, 2s30s 15.9bp, 5s30s 21.2bp, 10s30s 12.2bp, 2s5s -5.3bp. 2s10s steepened from 0.3bp on 19/11.

Treasury curve levels on 20/11/2026: 2s10s 29.7bp, 2s30s 68.1bp, 5s30s 58.9bp, 10s30s 38.5bp, versus long-run averages of 56.81bp for 2s10s and 90.35bp for 2s30s, so the curve remains flatter than history.
The report notes that extreme positioning and curvature may lead to near-term rate or curve changes. A high butterfly spread (long the belly) means the belly is cheap versus the wings.
risk_factors: Extreme positioning and curvature may drive near-term rate and curve changes, per the report summary.
